Zohran Mamdani's marquee plan as part of his 'tax the rich' agenda stalled again in a courtroom Tuesday after a judge accused the city of mishandling its rollout of the so-called 'pied-a-terre' tax.  The levy would impose an annual surcharge on wealthy property owners who do not primarily live in New York City with second homes worth more than $5 million. State Supreme Court Judge Wayne Ozzi of Staten Island ruled in favor of homeowners who sued the city, arguing it didn't work hard enough to figure out just who should be facing the tax before starting to collect.   'Homeowners are being substantially harmed and penalized needlessly by D.O.F.'s method of implementing the tax law,' Ozzi wrote.  Ozzi hit out at the city publishing a list of almost a million properties that could face the tax, including the names of the approximately 17,000 owners.  The tax - which was signed into law by Democrat Governor Kathy Hochul - remains legal but is now in flux, as it is no longer apparent how the city will collect the money owed, which must be received by next spring. The judge said the city must now remove its list and replace it with a more limited one that only displays the properties facing it.  #news #politics #newyork #tax #mamdani

FLYDUBAI: O primeiro-ministro de Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmou que o copiloto que atacou o comandante de um voo da Flydubai foi preso e será interrogado pelas autoridades sauditas. Segundo Netanyahu, um dos pilotos esfaqueou o outro durante o voo, quando a aeronave se aproximava de seu destino. “Aparentemente, ele tentou derrubar o avião com seus ocupantes”, afirmou o primeiro-ministro em uma mensagem em vídeo. O suspeito seria o copiloto da aeronave e, segundo autoridades israelenses, é cidadão de Omã. Um passageiro teria ajudado a imobilizá-lo após o ataque, enquanto outros integrantes da tripulação conseguiram assumir o controle e estabilizar o avião. While criticizing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Netanyahu referred to political commentator Hasan Piker and said that Piker had previously made the statement about the September 11 attacks. Netanyahu used the reference while questioning Mamdani’s associations and political views during his wide-ranging UN speech. The comment quickly drew attention online, with shortened clips circulating that appeared to suggest Netanyahu himself had made the statement. The full context shows that Netanyahu was quoting Piker rather than endorsing the remark. Reports also note that Piker has previously explained his comments as referring to the consequences or “blowback” of US foreign policy, rather than expressing approval of the deaths of 9/11 victims. What is Leftism? Who is a Leftist? *faces that pop-up:*Adorno, Proudhon, Sankara, Stirner, Marx, Parenti, Emma Goldman, Derrida, Luxemburg, Rousseau, Allende, Hegel, Richard Wolff, Bookchin, Gramsci, Angela Davis, Kohei Saito, Ernst Bloch, Kollontai, Frantz Fanon, Walter Benjamin, Lenin, Engels, Kropotkin, Fred Hampton, Ida B Wells, Horkheimer, Rick Roderick, Eugene Debs, Byung-Chul Han, David Graeber, Guy Debord, Mark Fisher, Che, Foucault, Jacques Lacan, Nietzsche, Mao, Judith Butler, Baudrillard, John Bellamy Foster,    What is the fundamental core of left-wing politics?  Leftism begins with humanity understanding itself as being on the same team. Society should be organised around meeting our shared and dependent interests, beginning with those whose needs are most urgent, rather than forcing everyone into endless competition for private property and profit.  This can be understood through the principle of triage. When resources, time and social capacity are limited, we should priorities people according to need. Those without food should be fed before someone acquires a tenth investment property. Those without housing should be housed before luxury apartments are left empty as financial assets. Those who are sick should receive treatment regardless of whether providing that treatment generates a profitable return. The point is not that everyone has identical needs, but that everyone depends upon a functioning society and upon the labor, knowledge, care and cooperation of countless other people.  The video begins with the bourgeois revolutions of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, when emerging capitalist classes challenged hereditary monarchy, feudal privilege and aristocratic rule. These revolutions produced though another unequal society.  Political power and economic power remains concentrated. The king could be removed, yet the workplace remained an authoritarian institution. Citizens might receive a vote in elections, but workers were given little or no meaningful control over the businesses, industries and productive systems that governed most of their waking lives.  Liberal democracy declared people politically equal when they weren't, while capitalism continuously reproduced material inequality.  A person may "idealistically" possess the same rights as a billionaire, landlord or corporate executive, but those rights operate inside a society where access to housing, healthcare, education, media influence, legal representation and political power is profoundly shaped by wealth. Formal equality therefore coexists with enormous differences in actual social power.  This contradiction is central to understanding the left.  Why do the people who perform the work rarely control what is produced, how it is produced, where the profits go or what conditions they work under? Why can a CEO, board of directors or group of distant investors make decisions affecting thousands of workers and entire communities without being democratically accountable to them?  Modern capitalism asks workers to accept a strange division: liberal "democracy" in the voting booth, hierarchy in the economy.  That "democracy" is a mythology.  You may vote periodically for representatives, but you spend much of your life inside institutions organised through commands from above. Your access to food, shelter and healthcare often depends upon obeying an employer. Your community may depend upon a company that can relocate, automate, downsize or close without the people affected having any meaningful vote.  Leftism proposes creating democracy on a material level instead of alienation. That can include trade unions, worker cooperatives, workplace councils, public ownership, community control, universal public services and democratic planning. Different leftist traditions disagree over strategy, but we just want to improve life as we know it.
